title: The Phoenicians and the Alphabet

cards.h: A tiny people who sold purple, sailed everywhere and gave us ABC
cards.b:
Phoenicia was a string of port cities on the coast of today's Lebanon: Tyre, Sidon, Byblos. No big empire. Just clever merchants with fast ships.

Their greatest export was not a thing you could hold. It was a way of writing.

Phoenicians made a dye from the murex sea snail. It took thousands of snails to dye one garment. The colour, Tyrian purple, became the mark of kings and later of Roman emperors.

The Greek name Phoinikes may come from the word for 'red' or 'purple'. The Phoenicians called themselves after their cities.

Before this, writing needed hundreds of signs (cuneiform, hieroglyphs). The Phoenician script had just 22 letters, each standing for a consonant. Anyone could learn it in days.

It developed about 1050 BCE from earlier scripts used by Semitic speakers in Egypt and Canaan (the Proto-Sinaitic script, about 1800 BCE).
About 800 BCE the Greeks borrowed it and used some letters for vowels. The first two letters, aleph and beth, became alpha and beta, giving us the word 'alphabet'.

Phoenician ships went across the Mediterranean and out to Spain and Atlantic Africa. They founded Cadiz in Spain and Carthage in North Africa. Tradition says Carthage was founded about 814 BCE by Queen Dido, who fled from Tyre. Dido is a legend; Carthage is real.

Herodotus said a Phoenician crew sailed round Africa for the Egyptian Pharaoh Necho II (around 600 BCE). Historians still debate whether that happened.

Carthage grew into a mighty sea power. It fought three wars against Rome, the Punic Wars (264-146 BCE). The great general Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants in 218 BCE.

In 146 BCE, Rome destroyed Carthage. 'Punic' is simply the Latin word for Phoenician.

cards.h: Did the Romans pour salt on Carthage?
cards.b: Myth: Rome sowed Carthage's fields with salt so nothing would grow.Fact: there is no ancient source for it. The salt story appears in the 19th and 20th centuries. Rome did destroy the city and enslave its people, which is bad enough without the legend.

Five things to remember

  1. Phoenicia was a group of port cities, mostly in today's Lebanon.
  2. The 22-letter alphabet was easy to learn.
  3. Greeks added vowels.
  4. Carthage was a Phoenician colony.
  5. Brahmi's origins are debated; Kharosthi came from Aramaic.

Think about it

  • Why would a simple alphabet change who can read?
  • What do Dido and Hannibal tell us about how Carthage was remembered?
